prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly TWO orthographic long-side edge profiles, RIGHT then LEFT, for the exact Iron Trains railcar metal edge-transition tile. The attached contact shows canonical source, accepted TOP, retained FRONT and current bottom/rear. TOP's four orange-brown bolted blocks arranged along the length axis (world Y) are authoritative. Preserve the square floor slab footprint and dark blue riveted steel with central narrow silver rail strip. FRONT and REAR are already approved/current and must not be regenerated; TOP and the plain BOTTOM remain unchanged.

RIGHT and LEFT cameras look horizontally at opposite long sides of the tile. Each candidate must show a thin low steel slab-edge cross-section across its length, a continuous dark-blue plate edge, a narrow silver rail line, and EXACTLY FOUR separate small orange-brown bolted support/block end faces spaced along the full Y length, corresponding one-for-one with the four rows of orange blocks in TOP. Four, not three. The silver rail follows the same long Y direction. All orange pieces stay low and attached; do not rotate the top pattern into a raised vertical panel or create posts. RIGHT and LEFT are opposite-side profiles and should reflect the same four fasteners across the steel body.

Keep total side span about 220px wide on the 256 canvas, edge thickness around 40px tall, bottom-aligned. Show no broad top hardware faces, no broad upright steel face, no ladders or extra bolts beyond the source structure. Crisp pixel-art clusters, transparent background, no labels, shadows, perspective, stray guide marks or clipping.
normalization: two alpha-connected row silhouettes extracted by full-atlas connectivity; uniform 220px width; bottom anchor y=248; NEAREST
